correctness.rationale: A stationary stochastic convolution, with position Brownian noise independent of stiffness Brownian noise, gives the two-time covariance as a positive integral of exp[-2 integral(past K)-integral(future K)]. The integrated OU covariance matrix has exact variance and cross-covariance formulas written in RESULT.md, yielding the claimed integral with A>0 exactly the finite-second-moment condition. Differentiating normalized Laplace expectations proves the two strict derivative signs, unique ordered critical thresholds, all endpoint and boundary cases, and absence of a maximum. A bounded tilted moment-generating function gives rigorous large-lag corrections; the beta-tilt implicit derivative gives the two weak-noise slopes. Independent 81-point quadrature/hypergeometric checks plus threshold-grid and OU-path Monte Carlo all passed, as corroboration only.

value.rationale: The existing OU-squared trap model has a physically meaningful stationary two-time observable that differs from the naive product of measured stationary variance and independently averaged impulse response. The theorem supplies an exact strict memory-excess inequality and a complete two-parameter qualitative classification of the relaxation envelope, including a unique-minimum window and a critical doubled exponential tail. These are natural dynamical response diagnostics, not an artificial finite slice or simple restatement of the established zero-lag moments.
